abstract: A recent study suggested a role of CHEK2 loss-of-function germ-line pathogenic variants in the predisposition to testicular cancer (TC) (AlDubayan et al. JAMA Oncol 5:514-522, 2019). We attempted to validate this finding relying on the high population frequency of recurrent CHEK2 pathogenic variants in Slavic populations. CHEK2 pathogenic alleles (c.1100delC (p.Thr367Metfs); del5395 [del ex9-10]; IVS2 + 1G > A [c.444 + 1G > A]) were detected in 7/280 (2.5%) TC patients vs. 3/424 (0.7%) healthy men and 6/1007 (0.6%) healthy women [OR 4.0 (95% CI 1.5-11), p = 0.009 for pooled control groups]. Somatic CHEK2 loss-of-heterozygosity (LOH) was detected in 4 out of 6 tumors available for analysis; strikingly all these instances of LOH involved inactivation of the wild-type allele. The CHEK2 c.470T > C (p.Ile157Thr) variant was detected in 21/280 (7.5%) affected vs. 22/424 (5.2%) non-affected men [OR 1.5 (95% CI 0.8-2.7), p = 0.3]. Somatic CHEK2 LOH was revealed only in 6 out of 21 tumors obtained from CHEK2 c.470T > C (p.Ile157Thr) carriers, with the C-allele lost in two cases and T-allele deleted in four tumors. The results of comparison of allele frequencies in TC patients versus population controls coupled with the data on CHEK2 LOH status in tumor tissues support the association of CHEK2 pathogenic variants with TC risk.
abstract_ja:
最近の研究では、CHEK2の機能喪失型生殖細胞系列病的変異が精巣がん(TC)の易罹患性に関与している可能性が示唆された(AlDubayan et al. JAMA Oncol 5:514-522, 2019)。我々は、スラブ系集団における反復性CHEK2病的変異の高い集団頻度に着目し、この知見の検証を試みた。
CHEK2の病的アレル(c.1100delC(p.Thr367Metfs)、del5395[del ex9-10]、IVS2+1G>A[c.444+1G>A])は、精巣がん患者280例中7例(2.5%)で検出され、健常男性424例中3例(0.7%)、健常女性1007例中6例(0.6%)と比較された[OR 4.0(95%CI 1.5~11)、併合対照群でp=0.009]。解析可能な腫瘍6例中4例で体細胞性のCHEK2ヘテロ接合性の消失(LOH)が検出され、注目すべきことに、これらのLOHはすべて野生型アレルの不活化を伴っていた。CHEK2 c.470T>C(p.Ile157Thr)変異は、罹患男性280例中21例(7.5%)、非罹患男性424例中22例(5.2%)で検出された[OR 1.5(95%CI 0.8~2.7)、p=0.3]。CHEK2 c.470T>C(p.Ile157Thr)保因者21例から得た腫瘍のうち、体細胞性LOHは6例にのみ認められ、C型アレルの消失が2例、T型アレルの欠失が4例であった。精巣がん患者と集団対照のアレル頻度の比較と、腫瘍組織におけるCHEK2のLOHの状況に関するデータは、CHEK2病的変異と精巣がんリスクとの関連を支持している。
